mix.evidence: The rental-and-price spine dominates the harvest: "sewa photobooth jakarta", "harga sewa photobooth jakarta", "photobooth jakarta murah" and "harga photobooth wedding jakarta" all sit in the top half by Suggest rank.
All five Jakarta administrative regions autocomplete independently (barat, timur, pusat, utara, selatan) plus "photobooth terdekat jakarta barat" and "photobooth jakarta kota".
A large branded-venue tail: "photobooth aeon jakarta garden city", "photobooth jakarta.starlight", "atedoz photobooth jakarta", "photobooth di mall ciputra jakarta".
Style and vendor comparison before booking: "best photobooth jakarta", "vendor photobooth di jakarta", "photobooth analog jakarta", "photobooth aesthetic jakarta".
Almost nothing. Only "buat photobooth jakarta" reads as a how-to, and even that is ambiguous between DIY and commissioning a custom build.

serpArchetype: Local pack over vendor listicles - a map pack of Jakarta rental vendors, then aggregator and directory pages, with almost no editorial content ranking

ruleDisagreements.why: "Kwangya" is a specific branded booth concept, not a product category. The searcher already knows which booth they want and is looking for that operator - price is incidental to finding the brand.

This is a photobooth operator sourcing their own equipment, not an end customer booking a booth. Same modifier, completely different audience - do not let it pull the consumer-facing pages off target.

strategistNote: This is a booking market wearing a browsing market's clothes: 38% of the harvest is already reaching for a price or a rental, and only one query in forty-one is genuinely informational. The thing to notice is the branded tail - Aeon, Starlight, Atedoz, Kwangya - which means a meaningful share of Jakarta searchers are hunting a specific operator by name. Content that competes on generic "photobooth jakarta" will lose to the map pack; content that competes on price transparency and area coverage will not.
